_readme: Known-dangling references inside sot/*.md, recorded 2026-08-28. This file may only SHRINK. CI rejects any PR that adds an entry. Burn-down is Station 05's job: fix the reference in sot/, then delete its entry here in the same PR. See docs/pipeline/stations/05-sot-keeper.md. TRAP 1 (MEASURED 2026-08-28 @82ba8538, RE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 @4461c8be): check-sot-refs.mjs resolves with existsSync against the WORKING TREE, so an entry can read as 'already resolved' on a dev box purely because its target is a gitignored local artifact -- the dev tree printed '17 baselined' while a clean worktree off origin/main printed '23' at the same SHA. Measure in a clean worktree, and before deleting an entry for a target you believe now exists, prove it: git cat-file -e origin/main:<path>. THE STRUCTURAL FLOOR WAS 8 AND IS NOT A FLOOR (2026-08-30, Station 05). Entries whose target is gitignored by design, or is a queue prompt the -ready.md-only EXCLUDED_PATH_CLASSES does not cover, are NOT burned down by deleting the entry -- deleting alone turns each into a hard CI failure (measured negative control: 10 entries removed, no markers, dangling=10 exit 1). They move from baselined= to exempt= by writing an inline <!-- sot-ref-allow: reason --> marker on the sot/ line itself. ALLOW_COMMENT_RE (check-sot-refs.mjs:154) is matched against the sot/ file's own line and continues BEFORE the path-class check and BEFORE existsSync, so the marker is the only mechanism that can clear a reference whose target is correct but structurally absent from main. It is also line-drift-proof, which a line-number-keyed baseline entry is not. It is Station 05's alone to write, because it lives inside sot/. TRAP 2 IS DEAD - DO NOT REINSTATE IT (RETIRED 2026-08-31, Station 05). It used to read: the ci.yml ratchet step grepped git diff for a + line containing missing_path, so deleting the LAST array element made the new last element drop its trailing comma, the diff showed that as an added line, and a PR that REMOVED ten entries was rejected for gaining one (MEASURED 2026-08-30, PR #1405, CI run 33316687892). Its instruction - never delete the last element - outlived its cause. PR #1407 replaced the grep with scripts/pipeline/check-sot-baseline-ratchet.mjs, which compares the SET of (sot_file, missing_path) pairs and the entry COUNT, deliberately ignores line numbers and array position, and runs a 4-case self-test (2 pass-cases, 2 fail-cases) on every invocation. VERIFIED 2026-08-31 at 6e105076 by reading ci.yml lines 201-217 and the script header. Deleting any element, the last one included, is now safe. The former last element (sot/README.md line 190 -> graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md) was cleared in the same run with an inline sot-ref-allow marker rather than a bare deletion, because its target is gitignored at .gitignore line 134 and has never been tracked - deleting the entry alone would have turned a baselined exemption into a hard CI failure. DO NOT write a count of remaining entries into this prose: entries.length is the count. Every sentence that has stated one here was stale within days. Every remaining entry needs a judgement call about a deleted doc or a moved source file, so none is auto-fixable. CLEARED 2026-09-03 (Station 05): the nine PROVENANCE-class entries were retired with inline sot-ref-allow markers, not deletions. Measured with two positive controls (CLAUDE.md = 5 commits, tender-client-notes.controller.ts = 2) that each of their targets has ZERO commits in origin/main history - they are documents of the predecessor workspace C:\Dev\ProjectOperations, folded in at the 2026-07-08 sot-consolidation, so there is nothing to repoint to and the citation is correct as provenance. What REMAINS is a different class: references to source files that moved or were retired inside THIS repo, where the sot/ prose makes a live technical claim. Those need a spec judgement, not a marker.
